summary: DeepSeek reportedly plans to train its next model on Huawei chips, Alibaba's chairman pitches open-source AI at Wuzhen, and a Jiangsu county builds a fake-nail industry.
body: DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI company, reportedly plans to train its next major model, V5, on Huawei's Ascend chips. The report comes from STAR Market Daily, a Chinese financial outlet, as relayed by TechNode, which could not confirm it [^1]. Until now, Huawei chips have mainly run DeepSeek's finished models, not the much heavier work of training new ones [^1]. If true, it is a real test of whether China can build top AI without American chips, which US export rules restrict. DeepSeek also released a prototype coding agent that watches developer group chats and suggests fixes unprompted; Digital Trends calls it "a prototype, not proof" that DeepSeek has passed US rivals [^2].

At the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen, Alibaba chairman Joe Tsai argued that open-source AI, models anyone can download and adapt, is the path to wide use, unlike the closed approach of many US firms [^3][^4]. Chinese state media says about 1,800 delegates from 138 countries and regions attended [^5]. A note of caution came from Hong Kong: Xiao Yuanqi, a vice head of China's financial regulator, warned that global AI investment is "overly concentrated" and raises borrowing costs for traditional industries [^6].

Daily life: Sixth Tone reports from Donghai County in Jiangsu, where online selling networks built for the crystal trade grew into a press-on nail industry with nearly 25,000 businesses by 2024, according to a local industry association [^7]. Workers paid by the piece earn 3,000 to 4,000 yuan (about US$450 to $600) a month, some shops livestream until 3 a.m. for overseas buyers, and one wholesaler estimates six or seven of every ten newcomers go out of business [^7]. My read: it is a small picture of China's export economy, fast and cheap, with very thin margins.

reads.title: Inside the Chinese County Selling $2 Nails to the World
reads.summary: A look inside a Jiangsu county's press-on nail boom: piece-rate work, late-night livestreams and fierce competition.
